# Commons Family — rules

Six cogs share one destructible resource for twenty simultaneous rounds. Every round each cog
splits three units of effort between TAKING from the resource and doing the thing that keeps the
resource alive, then everyone's choices settle at once. Taking pays you. Maintaining pays
everyone, including the cogs who did not maintain. That is the whole game, four times over.

## One round, in order

1. The engine snapshots the resource and sends every cog an observation.
2. All six decisions are made at the same time (one parallel batch of LLM calls, plus every
   scripted seat in-process). The round's hard deadline is 20 s; a 3 s pacing floor keeps an
   all-scripted episode watchable.
3. Each reply is clamped: integers to their ranges, colours to the enum, the effort budget
   enforced by reducing the MAINTENANCE field first, free text truncated on rune boundaries.
4. Chat is published. Messages attach to this round and become visible NEXT round — decisions
   are simultaneous, so no cog can read another's line before deciding.
5. The module resolves and pays out.
6. Sanctions apply, ascending slot: the payer loses 1.0, the target loses 3.0.
7. The resource regrows / silts / ripens / spawns, latching any permanent death.
8. Scores and the public ledger are booked and the round is recorded.

## Scoring

    score_i = sum of every module payoff you were paid
              - 1.0 x sanctions you paid for
              - 3.0 x sanctions you received

Higher is better. Every module payoff is non-negative, so a score only goes below zero when a cog
punished a lot or was punished a lot. The league ranks by these per-episode scores.

The grader is a separate, social-planner view: group welfare (all scores plus whatever the
commons still holds) divided by the module's planner optimum. It is not what the league ranks by.

## How an episode ends

- `complete` — all rounds settled. A dead orchard or six dead patches do NOT end the episode:
  the remaining rounds are played out, and the post-collapse scavenging is data.
- `deadline` — the wall-clock guard fired between rounds. Rounds already settled are scored as
  they stand and the process exits 0.
- `no_players` — no cog connected inside the connect timeout. All-zero scores, exit 0.

# The four modules

Each module is one `game_config.module` value: the same institutions, different resource physics.

## `cleanup` — Clean Up

One apple stock (starts 60, capacity 100) and one river. `harvest` takes apples; `clean` clears
silt. Apples regrow by `0.35 x (1 - pollution) x apples x (1 - apples/100)`. Pollution rises 0.12
every round and each clean unit removes 0.05, so holding it steady costs 2.4 units a round —
13 % of the society's whole effort, permanently, paid by whoever volunteers. Below 10 apples the
orchard is dead forever. Cleaning pays the cleaner nothing.

## `harvest` — Commons Harvest (open / closed / partnership)

Six patches, each up to 20 apples, starting at 12, regrowing at 0.40. Name one `patch`, demand
`harvest` from it. A patch left with less than one apple is DEAD FOREVER. Sustainable is 2.0 per
patch per round against a cap of 3 per cog — the temptation is exactly one unit wide.

- `open` — anyone may name any patch.
- `closed` — one patch per cog, publicly assigned; a demand by a non-owner yields nothing.
- `partnership` — two patches per pair, publicly dealt; a patch pays only if BOTH partners name
  it this round (either may demand 0 — naming it is holding it).

## `allelopathic` — Allelopathic Harvest

Sixty plant slots in red, green and blue, starting 20/20/20 with 6 ripe of each. `eat` ripe
berries of a colour, `plant` to convert a slot from the largest other colour. Each colour ripens
by `0.5 x planted^2 / 60` — quadratic in its own share, which is the inhibition: an even split
yields 10 berries a round for six cogs with 18 units of demand, a monoculture yields 30. Every
cog has a SECRET favourite colour that pays it 2.0 instead of 1.0, exactly two cogs per colour.
The good outcome needs four of six to eat a colour that pays them half as much.

## `mushrooms` — Externality Mushrooms

Red, green and blue mushrooms, 8 of each, three new ones a round weighted by what has been
eaten. Red pays +1.0 to the eater. Green pays +2.0 split among all six. Blue pays +3.0 split
among the five who did NOT eat it — the eater gets nothing. Eating k mushrooms freezes you for
k rounds. Blue is worth three times red to the group and nothing at all to you.

# Institutions

The layer around the resource is the same in every module, and each variant switches it.

- **Public ledger** (`ledger_public`) — every cog's alias, cumulative extraction, cumulative
  maintenance effort, its last five compact actions and its sanction counters. With the ledger
  off, only the aggregate taken last round survives: the no-reputation control.
- **Costly sanctions** (`sanctions_enabled`) — one target per cog per round. The payer loses 1.0
  and the target loses 3.0. Welfare-negative on purpose.
- **Posted norm** (`norm_text`) — one line in every observation and in every LLM system prompt.
  It binds nothing; it is a focal point.
- **Chat** (`chat_enabled`) — one signed public line per cog per round, at most 140 runes,
  visible in the NEXT round's observation and never inside its own.

Cogs address each other by anonymous alias (`Cog-A` … `Cog-F`), assigned by a seeded permutation.
Real policy names exist spectator-side only: in the replay, the results and the viewer. A cog can
never read who it is playing against.

Hidden from every cog: another cog's secret favourite colour, another cog's private note, any
decision for the current round, the episode seed, and the grader's optimum.

| variant | ledger | sanctions | chat | norm |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cleanup` | public | on | on | "one apple each, and someone cleans every round" |
| `harvest-open` / `-closed` / `-partnership` | public | off | on | none |
| `allelopathic` | public | on | on | none |
| `mushrooms` | public | on | on | none |

# Fielding a policy

One image, two environment variables. A policy is just a prompt.

    PLAYER_PROMPT="Take the sustainable share and no more..."   # an LLM seat
    PLAYER_SCRIPTED=steward                                     # a scripted seat

`PLAYER_SCRIPTED` wins when both are set. The player container registers its choice and then
spectates: every decision is made in the game container, so all six seats' LLM calls go out as
one parallel batch per round and a seat that cannot answer falls back to `steward` rather than
silently passing.

Scripted baselines: `steward`, `free_rider`, `cleaner`, `punisher`, `reciprocator`, `deterrable`,
`random`.

## Reply schema

One JSON object. Unknown keys are ignored, leading or trailing prose is tolerated.

| field | modules | type | range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `harvest` | cleanup, harvest | int | 0..3 |
| `clean` | cleanup | int | 0..3, `harvest + clean <= 3` |
| `patch` | harvest | int | 0..5 |
| `eat` | allelopathic, mushrooms | int | 0..3 |
| `eat_color` | allelopathic, mushrooms | enum | red / green / blue |
| `plant` | allelopathic | int | 0..3, `eat + plant <= 3` |
| `plant_color` | allelopathic | enum | red / green / blue |
| `sanction` | all | int or null | a cog slot 0..5, never yourself |
| `message` | all | text | at most 140 runes, public and signed |
| `note` | all | text | at most 200 runes, private, echoed back to you next round |

Anything out of range is clamped rather than rejected, and the effort budget is enforced by
reducing the MAINTENANCE field first — a greedy reply loses its cleaning, not its harvest.

readme.value:
# Commons Family

Six cogs share one destructible resource for twenty simultaneous rounds. Every round each cog
splits **three units of effort** between taking from the resource and doing the thing that keeps
the resource alive, and then everyone's choices settle at once. Taking pays you. Maintaining pays
everyone, including the cogs who did not maintain.

The resource physics come from one of four **modules**; the institutions around them — a public
ledger of who took what, costly punishment, a posted norm and one signed chat line per cog per
round — are the same in all four, and are switched per variant. That is the experiment: the
physics are the treatment, the institutions are the control.

| module | the resource | take | maintain | the trap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cleanup` | one apple stock + one river | `harvest` | `clean` | cleaning pays nothing; unclean → apples stop regrowing |
| `harvest` | six independent patches | `harvest` from a named `patch` | leaving ≥ 1 apple in a patch | a stripped patch is dead **forever** |
| `allelopathic` | 60 slots in three colours | `eat` ripe berries | `plant` a slot | ripening is quadratic in a colour's share, and your favourite pays double |
| `mushrooms` | red / green / blue mushrooms | `eat` a colour | eating green or blue | red pays you 1, green pays the group 2, blue pays *everyone but you* 3 |

Everything runs at an abstract round, not on a grid: a Clean Up cog does not walk to the river, it
spends one of its three effort units on `clean`. That is what keeps the planner optimum computable
and the game exactly solvable.

## Running one

```bash
docker build -t coworld-commons-family:latest .
tools/ci/docker_smoke.sh coworld-commons-family:latest   # one episode, six seats, raw docker
```

In-process, no containers:

```python
from coworld.examples.commons_family.game.engine import CommonsConfig
from coworld.examples.commons_family import headless

config = CommonsConfig(module="mushrooms", rounds=20)
state = headless.run_episode(
    config,
    headless.build_policies(["steward"] * 3 + ["free_rider"] * 3),
    parallel_seats=True,
)
```

## Fielding a policy

One image, env-switched:

```bash
PLAYER_PROMPT="Take the sustainable share and no more…"   # an LLM seat
PLAYER_SCRIPTED=steward                                   # a scripted seat
```

`PLAYER_SCRIPTED` wins when both are set. Baselines: `steward`, `free_rider`, `cleaner`,
`punisher`, `reciprocator`, `deterrable`, `random`. See `game/docs/player_protocol_spec.md` for the
reply schema, and the manifest's `policies.md` page for the short version.

## Where the LLM lives

In the **game** container, not the player container. Only the party that owns the round barrier
can issue all six seats' calls as one parallel batch, and only that party can enforce
retry-once-then-fall-back-to-scripted — otherwise a hung player pod silently becomes a passing
seat. The player container registers a policy and spectates.

## Layout

```
game/engine.py            the round loop, the institutions, the ledger, the replay document
game/modules/base.py      the module protocol: new_state / parse_decision / resolve /
                          dynamics / observe / residual_value / planner_optimum
game/modules/*.py         the four physics
game/llm.py               the LLM seat: credential ladder, one parallel batch, retry once
game/baselines.py         the seven scripted baselines, generalised across the modules
game/server.py            the Coworld game-container contract
player/player.py          registers a policy, then spectates
grader/commons_grader.py  welfare against the module's planner optimum
headless.py               in-process episodes, for the tests
shared/                   artifact IO and the log shipper, from coworld-meadow verbatim
```

Two name spaces, always: cogs address each other as `Cog-A` … `Cog-F` and can never read who they
are playing against; the real policy names live in the replay, the results and the viewer.

game.name: commons_family
game.description: Six cogs share one destructible commons for twenty simultaneous rounds. Four resource modules — a silting orchard, six patches that die if stripped, three berry colours that starve each other, and mushrooms that pay everyone but the eater — run on one institutional layer of public ledger, costly sanctions, posted norms and chat, so the experiment is the physics and the institutions are the control.

grader.name: Commons Social Planner Grader
grader.description: Scores an episode as group welfare divided by the module's planner optimum; reports survival, collapse round, dead patches, synchrony, extraction Gini and the public-effort share.

env.PLAYER_PROMPT: Take the sustainable share and no more: work out what the resource replaces each round, divide by six, take that. Spend an effort unit on the maintenance act whenever the resource is degrading. Say what your quota is and keep to it.

player.name: Commons Prompt
player.description: The reference prompt policy: an LLM seat whose whole strategy is its standing orders.

player.name: Steward
player.description: Takes a sustainable share and maintains when the resource needs it. The fallback every prompt seat drops to.

player.name: Cleaner
player.description: Spends one effort unit on the public good every round and stewards with the rest. The pure contributor, and exploitable.

player.name: Punisher
player.description: Stewards, and pays to burn the worst over-taker on the public ledger.

player.name: Free Rider
player.description: Takes the maximum every round and never maintains. The tragedy, distilled.

player.name: Random Cog
player.description: Uniform legal decisions. The maximum-variance control.

variants.name: Clean Up
variants.description: One orchard, one silting river. Cleaning pays nobody and keeps everybody fed. Public ledger, costly sanctions, a posted quota and chat.

game_config.norm_text: Posted norm: one apple each, and someone cleans every round.

variants.name: Commons Harvest (Open)
variants.description: Six patches anyone may pick from. Strip one below a single apple and it is dead forever. The no-property-rights arm of the A/B.

variants.name: Commons Harvest (Closed)
variants.description: The same six patches, one publicly assigned to each cog. Single-cog excludability: the middle arm of the property-rights A/B.

variants.name: Commons Harvest (Partnership)
variants.description: The same six patches dealt to three public pairs; a patch pays only if both partners hold it. The coordination arm of the A/B.

variants.name: Allelopathic Harvest
variants.description: Three berry colours that starve each other, and a secret favourite per cog that pays double. The good outcome needs four of six cogs to give up their preference.

variants.name: Externality Mushrooms
variants.description: Red pays you, green pays everyone, blue pays everyone but you, and eating freezes you. The instant-externality control case.
